# S365 — Local implementer: a cloud-written orientation pack in the brief

*Proposed.* Owner direction 2026-11-15 (relay session 8d711f67, chat: "I agree, go ahead"): before a local implementer starts, a cloud read-only role writes an orientation pack for the slice: for each failing test, the code to change and the nearest existing test to copy, quoted with file and line, and a short plan. ork puts the pack in the local implementer's brief so it edits instead of exploring. ## Why

*Proposed.* The cloud spec check already reads the slice's code to check its anchors (S258). Cloud tokens are cheap and fast for reading; local exploration is what fails. A pack of a few quoted functions is a few thousand tokens, against the 40k+ the local role spent per session re-reading.

Open owner questions (the implementer asks them with `adj ask` first):

- Q1 (`roles.local-orientation-writer`): which role writes the pack? (a) *recommended*: the spec check row, as one more output of the spec check that already runs before every run, only when the planned implementer is local. (b) a separate cloud read-only step after the spec check.
- Q2 (`roles.local-orientation-size`): how large may the pack be? (a) *recommended*: at most 300 quoted lines and 12k characters in all; the writer picks the lines. (b) no limit.
